Method of Attack: Data stealing Trojan designed to exfiltrate sensitive information including files, passwords, cookies, browser history, banking credentials, and cryptocurrency wallets
Acts as a downloader for other malware payloads in multi-stage campaigns
Poses as a signed Google Update installer using a stolen certificate
Achieves persistence by replacing the legitimate Google Updater program on compromised machines
Hides in plain sight by camouflaging as the Google Updater program to run with administrative privileges
Hijacks existing Google scheduled tasks and services to maintain persistence without altering Windows registry or adding new scheduled tasks
Impacted Systems: Windows machines with Google Updater installed
Attack Vector: Fake GoogleUpdate.exe binary signed with a stolen valid certificate issued to 'Singh Agile Content Design Limited'
Indicators of Compromise: GoogleUpdate.exe binary signed with a certificate issued to 'Singh Agile Content Design Limited' instead of Google
HTTP POST request to /index.php using a .bit domain (DNS over blockchain)
Mozilla/4.0 User-Agent string typical of AZORult infections
Presence of Google scheduled tasks: GoogleUpdateTaskMachineCore and GoogleUpdateTaskMachineUA
